title: Residual-based Adaptive Refinement of hp-Variational PINNs for elliptic PDEs with geometric singularities and localized features
authors: Somnath Giri, Muslim Malik, Rishikesh Yadav
abstract:
arXiv:2610.37670v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks approximate the solution of boundary value problems by minimizing the strong-form residual, their accuracy is often limited near corner and crack singularities, sharp layers and localized features and the enforcement of Neumann boundary conditions remains challenging. In hp-Variational Physics-Informed Neural Networks, the problem is formulated in a Petrov-Galerkin weak form, reducing the differentiation order applied to the neural network, while boundary constraints are imposed through penalty terms. The variational residual is evaluated using fixed Gauss quadrature points and the strong-form residual on a fixed collocation set, which may fail to capture regions of rapid variation. To address this issue, we integrate hp-Variational Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Residual-based Adaptive Refinement. During training, the strong-form residual is computed on a dense candidate pool and points with the largest residuals are added adaptively to the collocation set. Since the weak formulation is defined in $H^{1}(\Omega)$, it avoids the $H^{2}(\Omega)$ regularity requirement that fails on cracked and non-convex domains. The proposed method is validated on four two-dimensional elliptic problems and consistently achieves substantial reductions in relative $L^{2}$, absolute $L^{\infty}$ and relative $H^{1}$ semi-norm errors through adaptive residual-driven point placement.

title: Pooled Testing under Congestion: Operational Scaling Laws for Pool-Size Selection
abstract:
arXiv:2610.37729v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Classical pooled-testing rules choose pool sizes to reduce the number of tests. In practice, however, samples arrive over time, pools take time to form, testing capacity is finite, and positive pools create bursts of follow-up work. These operational features can make the test-efficient pool size far from the delay-efficient one.
  We formulate pooled testing with stochastic arrivals and finite testing capacity as a queueing system, and derive exact performance representations and asymptotic scaling laws for fixed-batch Dorfman testing and a dynamic two-threshold policy. The analysis reveals three distinct design regimes. When test usage is the main concern, the classical Dorfman rule is recovered and the optimal pool size scales with the inverse square root of prevalence. When delay accumulated while the laboratory is busy testing another batch matters, positive pools create service-time variability that grows more rapidly with pool size than the mean retesting burden, and the optimal scale shifts to the inverse cube root of prevalence. When waiting to assemble a pool is itself costly, the optimal fixed pool size remains bounded even as prevalence becomes very small. Under severe capacity scarcity, congestion remains relevant at the classical Dorfman scale: the square-root law survives, but with a capacity-dependent constant.
  Dynamic pooling separates two operational decisions that fixed pool sizes conflate. A lower threshold determines when routine testing should begin, while an upper threshold limits pooling when backlog is high. The lower threshold follows the cube-root scale, whereas the upper threshold primarily acts as congestion control. The results show how prevalence, capacity, and delay jointly determine pooling decisions and explain why operationally optimal pools can be much smaller than those suggested by test-efficiency calculations alone.

title: Nonlinear springs with orbits in radicals: a solvability criterion
abstract:
arXiv:2610.37730v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An odd polynomial oscillator has a periodic orbit given by a quadrature. When the zeros of the energy polynomial are all simple or all of even multiplicity, that quadrature is elementary exactly when the polynomial is a perfect square, and the time is a sum of inverse tangents. Recovering the displacement inverts that relation, algebraic when their coefficients are commensurate, making a closed form a Galois question. This paper identifies the group as the monodromy group of a rational map, computes its branch data from the parameters, and shows the branch value at the phase-angle singularity never vanishes, so every decomposition pairs the amplitudes reciprocally. In the commensurate family with distinct real factors, the orbit is radical exactly when the primitive inversion degree is at most four, or when reciprocal pairs leave a reduced spring of that degree. Radical orbits occur at the fifth, ninth, thirteenth and seventeenth force orders, the last only for reciprocal members, an expression recorded for each. The multiplicity hypothesis cannot be dropped. Factoring the energy polynomial into square and squarefree parts turns the quadrature into a differential of the third kind on a hyperelliptic curve, where elementarity is a torsion condition on the divisor of its poles with a vanishing holomorphic remainder. The first nonsquare elementary member appears at the ninth force order, and the power pullback inverts in closed form at every such order, giving a radical orbit for a confining spring of arbitrarily high degree with a sufficient condition for positive coefficients.

title: The Interference-Conjugate Transform: The Tightest Interference-Linear Surrogate for Power Control, Scheduling and Beamforming in Wireless Networks
abstract:
arXiv:2610.37794v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Closed-form fractional programming (FP), weighted MMSE (WMMSE), and the 2026 surrogate-enhanced methods SEFP and XMMSE all maximize the weighted sum rate by iteratively maximizing a surrogate linear in the interference power. We show that this family admits a unique best member: the interference-conjugate transform (ICT), which replaces each rate term $\log(1+a/b)$ by $\max_{\kappa\ge0}[\Omega(\kappa a)-\kappa b]$, where $\Omega$ is the closed-form partial convex conjugate of the rate in the interference variable and the optimal multiplier is the interference price $a/(b(a+b))$. We prove that, for any fixed price, $\Omega(\kappa\,\cdot)$ is the pointwise largest own-signal function compatible with a valid interference-linear lower bound, and that tightness at an anchor forces the price. Hence all four benchmark surrogates, which share this price and differ only in their own-signal term, are dominated pointwise by ICT. At SINR $\gamma$, the benchmarks' own-signal curvature exceeds the true curvature by factors behaving as $\gamma/2$ (FP/WMMSE) and $(\log\gamma)/2$ (SEFP/XMMSE), against $1+1/(\gamma(\gamma+2))$ for ICT, and this ordering carries over to the certified ascent per iteration and the asymptotic linear convergence rate. ICT yields closed-form updates at the benchmarks' per-iteration cost for single-antenna power control, uplink joint scheduling and power control, and multi-cell MISO beamforming, and the first solver-free algorithm for sum-least-$q$th-percentile rate maximization, via a $K$-dimensional convex dual with closed-form gradient and Hessian and a certified duality gap. In uplink scheduling, ICT improves proportional-fairness utility over FP by +7.03 and over SEFP by +3.35 (60/60 drops) using 18.7 iterations per slot vs. 49.7 and 38.0; in MISO beamforming with $M=8$, it reaches 99.9% of its final value in a median of 9 iterations vs. 16 (XMMSE) and 1160 (FP/WMMSE).

title: Characteristic identities for orthogonal quantum matrices: examples
abstract:
arXiv:2610.37813v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this note, we illustrate our recent results regarding structure theory of orthogonal Quantum Matrix algebras \cite{OP-BMW,OP-reciprocal,OP-ortho} using the simplest nontrivial example: the RTT-algebra associated with the canonical orthogonal R-matrix of type $O(3)$ (see, e.g., \cite{FRT}). By introducing a suitable linear order on the set of generators, we obtain a set of quadratic relations defining the algebra. Next, we investigate relations among its higher-degree polynomials. As a result, we verify `in components' the Cayley-Hamilton and the reciprocal relations, obtained earlier with the use of the R-matrix techniques. We explicitly calculate the coefficients of the characteristic polynomials of quantum matrices and propose a
  conjecture regarding the form of the Hilbert-Poincar\'e series for the RTT-algebra.

title: Optimality of Threshold Policies for Heat Storage Optimization and a Policy Gradient Algorithm
abstract:
arXiv:2610.37853v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the optimal control of a stylized finite-horizon heat-storage system operated by a prosumer who can buy heat from and sell heat to a district heating network. Heat production and consumption are uncertain, and charging and discharging decisions have to be taken before the subsequent heat balance is observed. The resulting problem is formulated as a Markov decision process with continuous state and action spaces. We first establish a structural characterization of the optimal policy as a two-parameter threshold policy. Under additional regularity assumptions, we prove differentiability and Lipschitz properties of the value functions.
  Exploiting the threshold structure, we parameterize the policy by the time-dependent lower and upper thresholds and derive a pathwise stochastic-gradient estimator. We then propose a projected stochastic policy-gradient algorithm, establish a constrained Kurdyka-\L ojasiewicz inequality and derive global finite-sample bounds for both the objective optimality gap and the distance to the optimal threshold vector. Finally, numerical experiments for a non-stationary heat-balance process illustrate the evolution of the threshold parameters.

title: Wasserstein Bounds for Euler and Randomized Midpoint Langevin Sampling with Noisy Gradients
abstract:
arXiv:2610.37858v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Stochastic-gradient Langevin methods are sampling algorithms that replace the gradient of the log probability density by a noisy, possibly biased evaluation. We study how such gradient-evaluation errors affect the Euler and randomized midpoint discretizations of Langevin dynamics by comparing each noisy chain with its exact-gradient counterpart. For continuously differentiable, strongly log-concave targets with globally Lipschitz gradients, we derive comparison bounds under a sub-Gaussian condition on the gradient noise. The resulting 2-Wasserstein bounds hold uniformly over iterations, and are linear in both the step size and the $L^2$ norm of the evaluation bias, with a square-root dependence on dimensionality. To the best of our knowledge, no comparable 2-Wasserstein bounds have previously been established for randomized midpoint with noisy gradients. For Euler, our results complement recent Wasserstein bounds by allowing biased evaluations, and by not requiring additional regularity assumptions on the evaluation errors.

title: A Poisson Transition and Bias Law for KSG Mutual-Information Estimation
abstract:
arXiv:2610.37941v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We quantify the error of the strict-radius Kraskov--St\"ogbauer--Grassberger (KSG-1) mutual-information estimator on a Gaussian channel as the sample size \(n\) grows and the channel becomes nearly deterministic. For fixed dimension \(p\) and neighbor index \(k\), we define the resolution parameter \(u_n=ne^{-I_n}\), where \(I_n\) is the true mutual information in nats. When \(u_n\to u\in(0,\infty)\), we prove that the estimation error converges in mean square to a computable deterministic bias \(B_{p,k}(u)\). Sampling fluctuations therefore vanish, while an additive bias can persist. We derive this bias from an explicit marked-Poisson law for the neighborhood counts, characterize its small-\(u\) asymptotics, and show that it tends to zero as \(u\to\infty\). The same law describes how often neighborhoods saturate, meaning that they make the largest possible contribution to the estimate. The limiting saturation probability decreases continuously and strictly from one to zero, allowing a Gaussian-model bias correction on fixed critical intervals. Finite-sample experiments show substantial bias even when the true information lies below the estimator's logarithmic ceiling and saturated neighborhoods are rare. Saturation-based correction reduces estimation error in these experiments, though recovering the resolution parameter from the observed saturation fraction can remain difficult when saturation is rare.

title: A Stochastic LineseArch Method (SLAM) for Minimizing Expectation Residuals: Weakening Boundedness of Gradient
authors: Qi Wang, Uday V. Shanbhag, Yue Xie
abstract:
arXiv:2610.37947v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We establish convergence guarantees for the Stochastic LineseArch Method (SLAM) proposed and analyzed in Wang et al. (arXiv:2512.14979) for nonconvex composite stochastic optimization, retaining the iteration and sample complexity orders of the original analysis assuming neither the boundedness of true gradients nor the Lipschitz continuity of the convex nonsmooth term $r$. ChatGPT was used to assist in developing a key intermediate result. Under uniformly Lipschitz continuous and unbiased sampled gradients with uniformly bounded variance with mini-batch sizes proportional to the iteration budget, SLAM achieves an iteration complexity $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ and a sample complexity $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-4})$ for obtaining an iterate whose expected proximal-gradient residual norm is at most $\epsilon$.

title: Federated Learning for Semantic Communications over Multiple Access Channels
authors: Yalin E. Sagduyu, Tugba Erpek, Yi Shi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.37951v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper presents a federated learning (FL) framework for semantic communication (SemCom) over the multiple access channel (MAC), where multiple distributed transmitters simultaneously convey semantic information to a common receiver using end-to-end learned semantic representations. Semantic feature extraction, compression, wireless transmission, and semantic inference are jointly optimized through FL-based SemCom. Unlike conventional SemCom systems that train users independently, simultaneous semantic transmissions over the MAC enable concurrent training of multiple transmitters within the same transmission interval, thereby reducing training overhead and channel usage. Federated semantic aggregation is incorporated with shared and personalized encoder components, allowing transmitters with limited local training data to benefit from semantic representations learned from transmitters possessing larger datasets while preserving local adaptation. Evaluated using the CIFAR-10 dataset over fading channels, the proposed approach maintains high semantic inference accuracy under shared wireless access and significantly improves performance under severe data imbalance. In the meantime, simultaneous semantic transmissions can significantly reduce training overhead while preserving robust semantic performance across distributed transmitters with heterogeneous local datasets. These results highlight the potential of combining FL and SemCom to support scalable and communication-efficient edge intelligence in future wireless networks.

title: Symmetry-resolved periods in a cyclic-dominance automaton: separating intrinsic from lattice-induced periodicity
authors: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no
abstract:
arXiv:2610.37990v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Periodic attractors of spatially extended systems possess not one period but a hierarchy of periods, one for each level of observation and symmetry quotient, and this hierarchy separates how a pattern evolves from how it fits the finite domain. For a synchronous threshold model of cyclic dominance on an $L\times L$ torus, equivalent to the three-color cyclic cellular automaton of Fisch, Gravner and Griffeath, we measure for every attractor a \emph{tuple} of periods: that of the populations ($\Tpop$), of the full configuration ($\Tst$), and of the configuration up to color rotations ($\Tcol$), lattice symmetries ($\Tgeo$) and the full space--color group ($\TG$). Equivariance implies exact divisibility relations and the factorization $\Tst=\TG\,m$, where $m$ counts the applications of the symmetry $h$ that maps the configuration onto itself after $\TG$ steps: $\TG$ and the type of $h$ belong to the pattern, $m$ to the lattice, and the attractors are relative periodic orbits whose full period emerges from the interaction between the intrinsic dynamics and the lattice symmetries. A family of attractors built around a pair of counter-rotating spirals, with $\Tpop=24$ and $\TG=8$, persists from $L=9$ to $L=40$ while $\Tst$ takes values from 24 to 960, given in every case by the order of $h$; on a rectangular $9\times12$ torus it takes the value 48, absent from all square tori. With more than $4.5\times10^5$ runs at each of $L=8$ and $L=9$ we estimate the basins of attraction: fixed points take 95--97\% of the configuration space, and no single period is enough to tell the oscillating attractors apart. The same analysis locates local diversity: it is balanced whenever the cycle has a color symmetry and, on large lattices, it is concentrated at the spiral cores.

title: Inexact PDHG for Large-Scale Semidefinite Programming
abstract:
arXiv:2610.37998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: First-order methods, such as the primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method, have recently been explored for large-scale semidefinite programming (SDP). However, exact projections can be computationally prohibitive, motivating inexact projections using conditional gradient methods. Although computationally cheap and projection-free, these methods typically converge sublinearly. Recent variants, such as Spectrahedron Frank-Wolfe (Garber, 2026), achieve linear convergence in expectation near the optimal face of the spectrahedron. We develop an inexact PDHG framework with tractable spectrahedral projections using two techniques: (i) adaptive error tolerances that avoid unnecessary inner iterations while guaranteeing convergence, and (ii) a heuristic spectral warm start based on the Lanczos algorithm that accelerates Spectrahedron Frank-Wolfe by initializing near the optimal face. We establish an O(1/t) convergence rate for PDHG in the presence of projection errors and estimate the total number of inner iterations required for convergence. Experiments on large-scale SDP instances demonstrate that combining spectral warm starts with Spectrahedron Frank-Wolfe outperforms Lanczos-based inexact projections.

title: On the $b$-Symbol Weight Distribution of Dual Melas Codes and a Poisson Randomness Postulate
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38017v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove a new lower bound on the $b$-symbol weight of codewords in dual Melas codes, which is strictly better than known results. We employ a new strategy that translates a pattern counting problem in linear-feedback shift register sequences to a problem on orbits of binary polynomials under a certain action. We use the same techniques to provide an improved lower bound on the burst-covering radius of Melas codes and a new upper bound on the critical exponent of dual Melas codes.
  We then define a new randomness postulate on (families of) binary sequences, based on the definition of infinite Poisson generic sequences. We conjecture that codewords in the dual Melas code satisfy this postulate, and we show partial progress in establishing this conjecture. We also show how a relaxed version of the problem can be completely resolved, and relate the conjecture to the first part of the paper, giving a justification of why the improved bounds on the $b$-symbol weight were somewhat to be expected.

title: An Improved Johnson Bound for List-Decoding with Hints
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38022v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper studies when list-decodability guarantees for error-correcting codes of good distance can go beyond the classical Johnson radius and gives a corresponding efficient list-decoding algorithm for Reed-Solomon codes up to this new radius. The Johnson bound shows that any error-correcting code with distance $\delta$ is automatically list-decodable with small list size up to a certain radius $J(\delta)$ around any received word $r$. We show that if the received word $r$ is known to have some codewords that are somewhat close to it (we call these ``hints"), then $C$ is list-decodable with small list size up to an even larger radius around $r$.
  We determine the optimal list-decoding radius in this setting for single and multiple hints over both large and small alphabets and show that this radius is the optimum of a natural convex program. Remarkably, even a single hint that is $(J(\delta)-\epsilon)$-close to $r$ improves the list-decoding radius around $r$ to $J(\delta)+\epsilon'$.
  Finally, we give an efficient algorithm, based on the weighted Guruswami-Sudan decoder, that list-decodes Reed-Solomon codes up to this optimal radius.

title: Trajectory-Planning Attitude Control System for Satellites with Magnetic Attitude Control and One Reaction Wheel
authors: Patrick McKeen, Alex Meredith, Kerri Cahoy
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38029v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Selecting attitude actuators for spacecraft in low earth orbit (LEO) often involves a trade between reaction wheels and magnetorquers. Reaction wheels generally have higher size, weight and power as well as cost, compared with magnetorquers, but have performance advantages. We consider a hybrid system relying on a single reaction wheel and three magnetorquers, using a trajectory planning control method that focuses on meeting pointing goals and minimizing the need to desaturate the reaction wheel. The use of planning allows for intelligent use of the reaction wheel and accommodates time-changing goals and orbit-varying magnetic fields. Preliminary results show trajectories with fractional-degree-accuracy, as well as management of reaction wheel momentum and avoidance of stiction. We also compare to a magnetorquer-only planning-based control system and show better convergence and faster slews.

title: Convergence analysis of an augmented dual-mixed fnite element method with skew-symmetric Nitsche stabilization for the generalized Oseen equations with mixed boundary conditions
authors: Cristian C\'arcamo, Abner Haguit Poza, Ramiro James Rebolledo
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38032v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyze a new skew-symmetric Nitsche-augmented mixed scheme for the generalized Oseen equations with non-solenoidal convective fields, subject to mixed boundary conditions. The scheme is based on a continuous pseudostress-velocity augmented dual-mixed finite element formulation, in which the Dirichlet datum is imposed naturally, whereas the prescribed normal trace of the pseudostress is incorporated into the $H(div,)$ stress space. We establish the well-posedness of the continuous formulation by means of a classical lifting argument and its corresponding homogeneous problem. The essential boundary condition is then weakly enforced in the discrete scheme through suitable stabilizing Nitsche terms. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution to the discrete scheme, allowing the use of general conforming approximation spaces for both the pseudostress and the velocity. Moreover, in the case of homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and general Neumann data, we establish the stability of the Nitsche scheme. Under mild regularity assumptions on the exact solution, we prove optimal convergence rates in an energy norm. Finally, numerical experiments in two and three dimensions confirm the theoretical convergence rates and assess the performance of the proposed scheme for non-solenoidal convective fields and solutions exhibiting boundary layers.

title: Conformal Predictive Distributions for Contextual Order Fulfillment Optimization
authors: Tinghan Ye, Amira Hijazi, Pascal Van Hentenryck
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38046v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ship-to-home fulfillment requires a retailer to select a fulfillment location and carrier before the delivery time is known. These decisions often rely on static transit-time estimates, which cannot represent how delivery-time uncertainty varies across orders and fulfillment options. This paper constructs conformal predictive distributions (CPDs) using Conformal Predictive Systems (CPS) for regression and the cross Venn-Abers predictor (CVAP) for multiclass classification, and uses them in a contextual optimization model for fulfillment decisions. The model is solved by contextual sample-average approximation (C-SAA). The regret of each fulfillment decision, its expected cost above that of the best decision, is bounded by forecast error, scenario-evaluation error, and the candidate-generation gap. The forecast term depends on how well calibration residuals or class probabilities represent the current order. On more than five million proprietary order records, CVAP raises exact-day accuracy from 49.5% for the rule-based estimate to 64.1%. Paired with a decision rule that selects a quantile weighting late errors more heavily, the split CPS (SCPS) gives a point estimate that raises late-delivery detection from 3.8% to 79.4%. Residual-based CPS distributions also meet or slightly exceed nominal interval-coverage targets. In decision experiments with a JD.com simulator over six test dates, C-SAA with CVAP lowers mean total cost by 7.1% and C-SAA with the Mondrian CPS (MCPS) lowers it by 6.7%, relative to C-SAA with the original nonconformal forecast. Both cut the late-delivery rate from 5.7% to below 4.0%.

title: An Energy-based discontinuous Galerkin method for the Westervelt equation with absorbing boundary conditions
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38058v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper develops and analyzes an energy-based discontinuous Galerkin method for the Westervelt equation in the acoustic-velocity-potential formulation with spatially varying material parameters and nonlinear absorbing boundary conditions. The semi-discrete scheme is constructed from the underlying energy balance and incorporates an additional consistent term to accommodate the strong damping operator within the discrete energy framework. Numerical fluxes are designed at both interelement and physical boundaries to provide a unified treatment of interior and boundary dissipation. For the nonlinear analysis, we study an auxiliary variable-coefficient linearized problem and establish stability and a priori error estimates, including the additional terms induced by the solution-dependent absorbing boundary flux. These estimates are combined with a fixed-point argument to prove existence, uniqueness, and convergence of the nonlinear semi-discrete approximation under suitable regularity, smallness, and nondegeneracy assumptions. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical convergence results and illustrate the performance of the proposed method.

title: Neural Stream Function Method for Electrical Impedance Tomography with Lipschitz Conductivities
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38064v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) reconstructs the conductivity inside an object from voltage and current measurements on its boundary. The resulting inverse problem is nonlinear and severely ill-posed. Neural networks offer a flexible computational approach, but training physics informed neural networks for EIT and relating their training loss to reconstruction accuracy remain challenging. We develop a novel constrained neural stream function method for planar EIT with Lipschitz conductivities. The method builds the conductivity constraints and prescribed boundary voltages into the neural trial functions and replaces the second order conductivity equation with a first order system in strong form. The measured current is also used to construct a fixed baseline for the stream function. For this formulation, we derive error estimates that relate the sampled neural objective to errors in the physical boundary currents and the reconstructed conductivity. The error estimates separate the contributions from neural approximation, measurement noise, and sampling. Numerical experiments further demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high reconstruction accuracy with both exact and noisy boundary data.

title: Neural Compression of Long ADMM Trajectory for Multiparametric Quadratic Program
authors: Liang Wu, Honghui Zheng, Bo Yang, Xu Yang, Yilin Mo, J\'an Drgo\v{n}a
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38079v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Solving large-scale multiparametric quadratic programs (mpQPs) in real time often requires thousands of iterative optimization updates, creating a major computational bottleneck in model predictive control and learning-enabled systems. This paper proposes TQPNet, a self-supervised neural compression framework that learns to compress long ADMM optimization trajectories into a compact neural warm start followed by a few refinement iterations. We derive a low-dimensional ADMM scheme operating on the primal-dual variables $(x,\beta)$ and show that its iteration admits an equivalent ReLU-layer representation, termed ADMM(ReLU). Building on this insight, TQPNet combines a multilayer perceptron with ReLU activations (MLP(ReLU)) and a small number of unrolled ADMM(ReLU) refinement layers. The network is trained offline using an optimality-condition-informed residual loss, eliminating the need for solver-generated labels. The proposed residual-based framework enables both self-supervised training and online solution certification through adaptive ADMM(ReLU) refinement. Experiments on large-scale mpQPs and real-time MPC applications demonstrate that TQPNet achieves high accuracy, strong generalization, and substantially faster inference than conventional optimization-based methods.

title: Boxing Problem
authors: April Niu, Santanu Dey, Oktay G\"unl\"uk, Jisun Lee
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38085v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the \textit{Boxing Problem}, which seeks a subset of points in \(\mathbb{R}^d\) maximizing the total reward of a selection of points minus the width of its axis-aligned bounding box. We also investigate the associated \textit{Boxing Set}, defined by the epigraph of the width function over binary selection variables. Although the width function is not submodular in general, we restore submodularity by fixing an anchor point. After anchoring, we establish a connection to the intersection of mixing sets with a linking constraint, which yields a polynomial-time optimization algorithm and a polynomial-size extended formulation. We then study the polyhedral structure of the Boxing Set and show that its facets admit laminar families of tight sets and can be obtained by sequential lifting. For the one-dimensional case, we provide a complete description of facet-defining inequalities together with a strongly polynomial-time separation algorithm.

title: TensorSpectra: Bridging the Spectral and Tensor Worlds for High-Dimensional PDEs
authors: Bingcheng Hu, Tianchi Yu, Zhaoxiang Li, Ivan Oseledets
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38087v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) remain challenging for spectral methods due to the exponential growth of multidimensional coefficient spaces. We propose TensorSpectra, a low-rank spectral framework that directly parameterizes spectral coefficient tensors in canonical polyadic (CP) form, reducing representation complexity from $\mathcal{O}(N^d)$ to $\mathcal{O}(dNr)$. TensorSpectra combines structure-preserving spectral calculus, de-aliased nonlinear interactions, operator-aware residual weighting, and progressive low-rank corrections to enable efficient PDEs solving in compressed coefficient space. We further establish a theoretical framework connecting spectral truncation, low-rank approximation, and optimization errors. Extensive experiments across five PDE families and 24 benchmark configurations demonstrate State-Of-The-Art accuracy among five representative baselines, with TensorSpectra consistently achieving the lowest relative $L^2$ errors. More broadly, our findings offer a new perspective on high-dimensional PDEs solving, suggesting that exploiting intrinsic low-rank structure in spectral coefficient space provides a viable alternative to conventional physical-space approaches.

title: Strong stable sets and asymptotic fineness
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38099v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We investigate the strong stable sets of the geodesic flow on hyperbolic surfaces and their relation to the injectivity radius. We prove that the strong stable set of a vector does not coincide with its stable horocycle if and only if the injectivity radius along the associated geodesic ray is not bounded away from zero and the ray does not diverge through a cusp. In that case, the strong stable set is an uncountable union of stable horocycles. In previous works, we considered the particular cases where the ray meets arbitrarily short closed geodesics or closed horocycles. Here we complete the study by treating the third possible case, where the ray meets closed hypercycles of arbitrarily small length.

title: Randomized algorithms in numerical linear algebra for scientific computing
authors: Ethan N. W. Epperly, Daniel Kressner, Yuji Nakatsukasa
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38157v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Randomized numerical linear algebra (RNLA) has fundamentally changed the landscape of scientific computing over the last twenty to thirty years. While early breakthroughs focused primarily on low-rank approximation and least-squares problems, randomized techniques are now used to solve a broad range of linear algebra problems, supporting applications spanning data science, optimization, and computational engineering. This paper surveys some of the main ideas of RNLA, focusing on methods that are effective in practice and on simple theoretical bounds that can be used to understand them. We highlight the core benefits of randomization: improved scalability, algorithmic simplicity, and---contrary to what the name may suggest---remarkable reliability and numerical stability. Topics include sketching, low-rank approximation, least squares, orthogonalization and approximate orthogonalization, randomized Krylov subspace methods, preconditioning, trace and spectral density estimation, row and column selection algorithms, posterior error estimation, randomized regularization, and tensor-structured randomness.

title: In-Context Learning for Multi-Fidelity Multiscale Model Closure and Cross-Operator Out-Of-Distribution Generalization
authors: Xinyuan Li, Matthew Zahr, Panos Stinis, Zecheng Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38179v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-fidelity learning uses low-fidelity information (coarse-scale PDE models) together with limited high-fidelity data (fine-scale solutions) to obtain high-accuracy PDE solutions. It is a data-driven approach to downscale reduced-order models to solve PDEs efficiently and accurately. Standard multi-fidelity learning focuses on one operator or PDE; given a new PDE, retraining using additional coarse-fine solution pairs may be required, which is costly. In this work, we propose an in-context multi-fidelity learning framework for learning multiple multi-fidelity operators with one shared model. The model is trained using paired low- and high-fidelity examples as demonstrations from multiple operators, together with a new coarse-scale solution query, to predict the corresponding fine-scale solution. Once trained, given a new PDE operator, a few (fewer than five) coarse-fine demonstration pairs, and a low-cost coarse query, the model predicts the corresponding fine-scale solution without fine-tuning. When the target operator appears in the training dataset but has a different prediction goal, such as predicting beyond the training time interval, no additional demonstrations are needed. Instead, the model uses training coarse-fine pairs from that PDE and information from other training operators. Testing then only requires generating a low-cost coarse-scale solution query, without fine-tuning. Notably, our smallest model contains only 255,364 trainable parameters, corresponding to approximately 456 parameters per training operator for 560 operators.

title: Scalable Bayesian Quadrature via Operator-Adapted Features
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38212v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Kernel methods face two recurrent bottlenecks: the cubic cost of inverting an $n\times n$ kernel matrix, as in kernel ridge regression, and the evaluation of kernel integrals, as required in kernel quadrature. Existing low-rank kernel and Gaussian process approximations primarily address the former bottleneck, but do not control the downstream quadrature error when both the kernel matrix and kernel mean are approximated, particularly when the integrand lies outside the kernel reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We address both challenges through an operator-adapted finite-feature approximation. Specifically, we construct a finite-dimensional working kernel from the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a second-order differential operator. We establish convergence guarantees for the resulting finite-feature estimators in kernel quadrature, with extension to other related kernel methods. Our results show that, with $m \lesssim n$ basis functions, the truncated estimator attains the corresponding benchmark statistical rates. The theory covers fixed/random designs, noisy/noiseless observations, oversmoothing/undersmoothing regimes, and Mat\'ern/Gaussian-type weights. We provide explicit error bounds that quantify the roles of the spectral cutoff, regularization parameter, lengthscale, sampling geometry, and operator boundary condition. We verify the convergence results in numerical experiments.

title: Bound-preserving and mass-conserving projection BCFD methods for incompressible miscible displacement in porous media
authors: Xiaoying Wang, Shusen Xie, Hongfei Fu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38219v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyze two novel structure-preserving projection schemes for the incompressible miscible displacement problem in porous media. These schemes are specifically designed to preserve two essential physical properties--concentration bounds and the mass balance identity, and are accompanied by a rigorous error analysis for the projection approach. Both schemes are second-order accurate in space but differ in temporal accuracy: one is first-order and the other is second-order. Methodologically, both schemes comprise a prediction step for the concentration variable, based on a second-order modified upwind discretization together with an implicit-explicit finite difference approximation, followed by a projection (or correction) step that enforces the desired physical constraints, namely bounds and mass conservation. For the first-order temporal scheme, the velocity and pressure are solved at the first step on staggered spatial grids with explicit treatment of concentration. In contrast, for the second-order scheme, to ensure well-posedness and to suppress non-physical oscillations in the simulation, the velocity and pressure are solved at the final step with the concentration treated implicitly. A rigorous numerical theoretical framework is established for the first-order scheme, encompassing optimal-order error estimates, stability, and proofs of the existence and uniqueness of the numerical solutions. The numerical analysis framework is further extended to the more involved second-order scheme, and the corresponding theoretical results are briefly outlined. Finally, numerical examples, including some 'real' simulations, are presented to verify the theoretical findings and demonstrate the strong performance of the proposed schemes. In particular, the occurrence of viscous fingering is successfully captured and confirmed by the numerical results.

title: Damped stochastic mirror descent for non-smooth ill-posed problems in Banach space
authors: Harshit Bajpai, Gaurav Mittal, Ankik Kumar Giri
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38258v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce a damped variant of the stochastic mirror descent method for systems of non-smooth nonlinear ill-posed operator equations in Banach spaces. At each iteration, the method samples a random subset of the equations, performs a mirror-descent step in the dual space with an adaptive step size derived from the discrepancy principle, and applies a damping term that prevents the iterates from drifting away from the initial guess. The scheme accommodates non-smooth forward operators through a family of bounded linear surrogates, admits general $p$-convex penalty functionals which also includes trained convex penalty, allows the noise level to differ from equation to equation, and dispenses with two classical requirements, namely reflexivity of the image space and G\^ateaux differentiability of the forward operator. We study its regularization properties under an \textit{a posteriori} stopping rule by proving first that the iteration terminates after finitely many steps almost surely, and then that the mean-square error of the iterates tends to zero as the noise level vanishes. Numerical experiments on a system of non-smooth semilinear inverse source problems and the identification of a diffusion coefficient confirm the theoretical analysis and shows improved convergence results.

title: Hybrid CutFEM-IFEM model for embedded and immersed interfaces with triply-cut cells for the 2D Poisson problem
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38271v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a hybrid CutFEM--IFEM method for 2D Poisson problems with an immersed fluid--fluid interface and an embedded fluid--solid interface on a single unfitted mesh. The proposed method leverages the strengths of both unfitted finite element methods and immersed interface techniques to handle complex interface geometries and strong discontinuities efficiently. A composite equivalent polynomial representation of the Heaviside and Dirac delta functions is used to integrate on triply-cut cells. Moreover, the IFEM basis functions are enriched with the lift functions exactly representing solution and flux jumps. Numerical examples show optimal convergence for linear and quadratic elements, with accuracy comparable to that of a mesh fitted to both interfaces.

title: Data-driven stochastic asymptotic regularization for ill-posed inverse problems with a posteriori and heuristic stopping
authors: Simran Soni, Harshit Bajpai, Ankik Kumar Giri
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38279v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A novel Data-driven STochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{D-STAR}) method is proposed for solving linear and nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems, which incorporates a data-driven drift and a stochastic diffusion mechanism. Both known and unknown noise level cases are accommodated by the method, thereby making the framework applicable to a broader range of practical inverse problems. For known noise level, a modified discrepancy principle is employed, whereas for unknown noise level, a heuristic stopping rule based solely on noisy data is developed. For each stopping rule, an appropriate diffusion term is defined and the well-posedness of the associated stochastic differential equation is demonstrated. The finite termination of \texttt{D-STAR} method under both stopping rules is established and its convergence to the exact solution in the noise-free setting is proved. For the noisy data, stability and the regularization property in the mean-square sense are further established. In addition, the uncertainty quantification of the proposed method and its comparison with the Stochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{SAR}) method under both rules are provided. Furthermore, it is shown that local minima arising in the Data-Driven Iteratively Regularized Landweber (\texttt{DDIRLI}) method may be escaped. Finally, detailed numerical experiments, including comparisons with existing \texttt{DDIRLI} and \texttt{SAR} methods, are presented on X-ray computed tomography and nonlinear schlieren tomography for both stopping rules, thereby demonstrating the performance of \texttt{D-STAR}.

title: Exact Second-Order Asymptotics for the Gaussian Gray--Wyner Problem
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38306v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We revisit the Gray-Wyner problem of lossy compression of bivariate Gaussian sources under the quadratic distortion measure and derive the exact second-order asymptotics. Specifically, we first identify the boundary rate tuples using the explicit first-order asymptotics by Yu (TIT 2023) and then characterize the tradeoff among three second-order coding rates subject to a constraint on the joint excess-distortion probability. Our main contribution is the achievability proof, where we derive a covariance shell covering lemma that is analogous to the type covering lemma for the discrete case. In particular, our covering lemma classifies the source sequences into power shell types via their empirical covariance matrix. For each such power shell type, we derive sufficient conditions on the compression rates so that covering within distortion levels are achievable. Finally, asymptotical analysis via the Berry-Esseen theorem yields the desired result.

title: Tight Stationarity Transfer and Repeatability for Inexact Proximal-Gradient Methods
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38310v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Proximal-gradient methods are widely used for composite optimization, but inexact proximal updates introduce a residual in the proximal optimality condition, complicating the analysis of how stationarity changes across a step. We study this question for composite objectives consisting of a smooth convex term and a possibly nonsmooth weakly convex term, focusing on the relationship between the directional-stationarity measures at the input and output points of an inexact proximal-gradient step. We first establish separate input and output bounds, but their combination can yield a conservative estimate because their worst-case residual directions may differ. By exploiting the magnitude and orientation of this shared residual, we establish tight joint bounds and derive an exact one-step stationarity-transfer factor that strictly improves the estimate from separate bounds in the short-step regime. We also identify the precise residual-tolerance threshold for finite uniform stationarity transfer. A further distinction emerges over multiple steps: endpoint worst cases can repeat over arbitrarily many iterations, whereas interior worst cases cannot persist across two consecutive steps, yielding strict two-step submultiplicativity. These results also provide principled tolerance-selection rules, descent estimates, and stationarity-complexity guarantees for inexact proximal-gradient methods.

title: The Minimax Complexity of Federated Optimization under Interpolation: The Role of Oracle Models
authors: Kirill Novoselov, Yuriy Dorn, Darina Dvinskikh, Alexander Gasnikov

title: A five-species counterexample to the Hofbauer--Kon--Saito conjecture on qualitative permanence
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38374v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Hofbauer, Kon and Saito (J. Math. Biol. 2008) showed that a Lotka-Volterra interaction matrix $A$ with negative diagonal can be qualitatively permanent only if (C1) every cycle of length $\ge 2$ of $A$ is nonpositive and (C2) every negative cycle contains exactly one negative entry. They conjectured that these conditions are also sufficient, and proved this for $n\le 3$. We give a $5\times 5$ integer matrix with seven nonzero off-diagonal entries that satisfies (C1) and (C2) but is not qualitatively permanent. For an explicit integer growth vector the system has an interior equilibrium, and an asymptotically stable heteroclinic cycle on the boundary of the orthant attracts an open set of interior orbits. Adding non-interacting species gives counterexamples for every $n\ge 5$. The interactions form a one-way feedback loop (two one-sided benefits and one one-sided harm) together with a predator of two prey. The verification is elementary except for one heteroclinic connection, which lies in a face that is not Volterra-Lyapunov stable. For it we prove a connection lemma based on invasion graphs.

title: Is Dual Polarization Always Optimal? Unlocking New Spatial Degrees of Freedom
authors: Adrian Agustin, Xavier Mestre, Carlos Su\'arez Garc\'ia, Alberto Pellon Sancho
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38377v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Current wireless communication systems are designed based on channel models obtained under the assumption of far-field operation, where electromagnetic waves can be approximated by a planar wave. In those circumstances, dualpolarized antennas seem to be the optimal solution for maximizing the spectral efficiency. However, the recent research on XLMIMO systems represents a paradigm shift, since communication may take place in the near-field and an additional degree of freedom can be achieved. This work presents a modular, lowcost tripolarized antenna at 2.4 GHz band, that is used to experimentally validate theoretical findings about tripolarized antennas, which are commonly based on orthogonal infinitesimal dipoles. The evaluation is carried out in two indoor scenarios and one outdoor scenario, with transmitter comprising multiple tripolarized antennas and a receiver equipped with a single tripolarized antenna. We show that this type of antenna can increase the number of spatial streams up to three or extend the region where terminals are able to achieve two spatial streams

title: Using delays for prescribed-time static output feedback stabilization of LTI controllable and observable systems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38417v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper addresses a stabilization problem: can every controllable and observable LTI system be stabilized by static output feedback? To the best of our knowledge, we provide, for the first time, a solution to this problem. Furthermore, the proposed design achieves prescribed-time convergence to the origin, with the convergence time arbitrarily assigned a priori and independently of the initial condition. Two static output-feedback methods are developed. The first employs multiple artificial output delays with smooth time-varying gains and provides an explicit gain construction for every controllable and observable LTI system, based on a generalized controllability--observability Gramian introduced in this paper. The second combines constant-gain feedback of the current output with time-varying-gain feedback of a single artificially delayed output and also applies to every controllable and observable LTI system. Its simpler structure requires auxiliary parameters whose existence is guaranteed but whose explicit construction is not provided for general MIMO systems; for SISO systems, the constant current-output gain can be readily selected. The multiple-delay design is further extended to known bounded and fast-varying (without any constraints on the delay derivative) measurement delays, yielding fixed-time stabilization under a corresponding rank condition, with an assignable settling-time bound greater than three times the delay bound. For unknown constant measurement delays, fixed-time stabilization is established for systems with nilpotent state matrices. A numerical implementation is also presented. Numerical examples involving nonminimum-phase, flexible-structure, and cart--pole systems illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

title: Polynomial-Time Constructions of Asymptotically Good Random Access Codes from Linear Codes
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38429v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Random access codes (RACs) encode a $q$-ary input string into fewer $q$-ary symbols while allowing any requested input symbol to be recovered with probability above the random-guessing value $1/q$. However, it remains unclear what asymptotic guarantees on compression and recovery probability should be required of RACs. We address this question by introducing the notion of asymptotically good RACs and give two polynomial-time constructions. First, an $[n,k,d]_q$ linear code with $d\ge2$, together with an encoder based on its orthogonal-array property, yields an $(n,n-k)_q$-RAC with worst-case decoding success probability \[ p_{\rm wc}=\frac{1}{q}+\left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right)\frac{d-2}{n}. \] These OA-RACs are asymptotically good whenever the underlying linear codes are, and Garcia--Stichtenoth algebraic-geometry codes give a concrete polynomial-time realization. Second, a direct-sum strategy using OA-RACs derived from $q$-ary Hamming codes and the trivial $(1,1)_q$-RAC yields asymptotically good RAC families at every prescribed RAC rate $R_{\rm RAC}=(n-k)/n\in(0,1)$. Numerical results demonstrate favorable finite-length performance of both constructions.

title: Optimal approximation error approach in Bayesian inverse problems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38434v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In many inverse problems, evaluating the forward operator is computationally expensive, making it common practice to accelerate inference with a less costly approximate model. However, such approximations introduce unwanted bias and must be carefully accounted for to ensure the reliability of the solution. This phenomenon is particularly pronounced in Bayesian inference, where accurate posterior characterisation typically requires a large number of forward model evaluations. In this paper, we focus on the approximation error model (AEM), which compensates for the modelling error by adjusting the likelihood density. More precisely, AEM incorporates the model error into the additive Gaussian noise distribution. A central challenge in this approach is how to choose the modified noise mean and covariance in a principled way. To address this, we propose a new framework, optimal approximation error (OAE) which determines the noise model by minimising the expected information loss, measured via the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the true and approximate posterior distributions. We show that the standard enhanced error approach (EEA) is recovered as the minimiser of the expected divergence between likelihoods rather than posteriors and develop OAE as a direct alternative targeting posterior accuracy. We establish bi-convexity of the OAE objective, introduce a regularised, provably convergent proximal alternating minimisation scheme, and derive closed-form expressions in the Gaussian linear setting. We further show that OAE estimates computed from empirical training data are statistically consistent. Numerical experiments on a linear CT problem and a nonlinear Darcy-flow problem show that OAE improves posterior accuracy relative to both the uncorrected and EEA-corrected likelihoods.

title: MacKay-Neal Codes for DNA Channels under Block-MAP Decoding
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38440v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove achievability below the symmetric information rate (SIR) under block maximum a posteriori (MAP) decoding for a fixed-degree MacKay-Neal (MN) socket ensemble on the quaternary insertion-deletion-substitution channel used to model DNA reads. For every integer $\ell\ge4$, the $(\ell,3,3)$ socket ensemble, with one transmitted bit fixed and an independent uniform known offset, has limiting rate $r_\star=6/\ell$ bits per stored nucleotide. If the joint SIR $J_t$ of a fixed number $t$ of reads under independent, uniformly distributed input nucleotides exceeds $r_\star$, the ensemble-average full extended-word block error is $O(1/n)$, and deterministic graph-offset sequences attain the same limiting rate and message-average error bound. This result concerns the discrete rate family $6/\ell$, not arbitrary rates approaching a given SIR. The channel permits arbitrarily many insertions and unbounded drift, with no alignment supplied to the receiver. The proof combines established MN parity and distance estimates with a strict arbitrary-candidate-list bound and a list construction that accounts for hidden output boundaries.

title: A $\pi / 4$ lower bound for random access in symmetric linear ensembles under optimal decoding
authors: Daniella Bar-Lev, Ohad Elishco, Ryan Gabrys
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38446v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the expected number of random linear observations required to recover a prescribed information symbol. For ensembles with uniformly random supports, independently sampled nonzero coefficients, and uniformly bounded column weights, we prove that the asymptotic normalized expected recovery time is at least $\pi/4$ under optimal decoding. The result holds over finite or infinite fields and extends the lower bound previously established for binary fully symmetric codes under peeling decoding. For singleton - pair observations, we determine the exact limiting expectation and show that optimal and peeling decoding have the same limit, independently of the field and coefficient distribution. The minimum within this family is approximately $0.793933445$, which explicit constructions attain asymptotically over every fixed finite field.

title: Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receiver Empowered Hybrid Non-orthogonal Multiple Access
authors: Xinya Shen, Zheng Chu, David Chieng, Chiew Foong Kwong, Qihao Peng, Pei Xiao, Theodoros Tsiftsis, Jianyue Zhu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38451v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel uplink Hybrid Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) architecture assisted by Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receivers (RAQRs) to improve energy efficiency by addressing the physical constraints of atomic sensing. We formulate a joint optimization problem encompassing phase measurements and multi-user power allocation to minimize the total transmit power. This problem is particularly challenging due to the non-linear amplitude-only observations of atomic vapor cells. To decomposes the resulting non-convexity, we develop a hierarchical three-layer decomposition optimization framework that systematically decouples the global problem. The inner layer employs a customized Expectation Maximization-Gerchberg-Saxton (EM-GS) algorithm to resolve phase ambiguity and estimate equivalent channel gains. The middle layer derives closed-form optimal power allocation solutions via Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions. The outer layer utilizes linear Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) detection for high-reliability signal recovery. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework over conventional RF-based Hybrid NOMA. Notably, the atomic architecture achieves approximately a 93% reduction in total power consumption compared to Orthogonal Multiple Access (OMA) baselines while maintaining strict backward compatibility, thereby laying a solid foundation for practical deployment in next-generation green communication networks.

title: Notes on Orlicz Spaces and Interpolation
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38455v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Orlicz spaces are a natural generalization of classical Lebesgue spaces. They are built upon convex growth functions and provide a flexible framework for studying integrability conditions beyond power-type behavior. In this survey paper, we present the basic definitions, main properties, and fundamental results concerning Orlicz spaces, and also discuss the Marcinkiewicz interpolation result for Orlicz spaces.

title: Stable Dynamical Mass Transportation via port-Hamiltonian Structure
authors: Dongjun Wu, Yankai Lin, Gang Feng
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38465v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Dynamical optimal mass transportation over nonlinear systems is often hindered by the curse of dimensionality and open-loop implementation. We propose an alternative framework that sacrifices exact optimality in favor of stability, robustness, and scalability. We use a stochastic port-Hamiltonian system as a reference model. Under suitable structural assumptions, we show that its density converges asymptotically to a prescribed steady-state distribution. We then shape a deterministic nonlinear system into a compatible port-Hamiltonian form and add a local density-feedback term so that its closed-loop continuity equation matches the Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation of the reference model. The resulting feedback drives a broad class of initial distributions to the target distribution. Because the density term is local at the particle level, the controller admits decentralized implementation and avoids solving a global finite-horizon transport problem online. Nonlinear examples and simulations illustrate the method. For linear systems with Gaussian targets, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for stabilizing density feedback and give explicit controller constructions.

title: Beyond Reachability: When Edit Order Preserves Couplings in Graph Flow Matching
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38486v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Shortest-path optimality does not guarantee that a memoryless graph generator preserves a prescribed source-target correspondence. We study whether reordering legal shortest edits can retain this correspondence without changing the pairing, mandatory edits, or sampling budget. Under a common Poisson clock, we establish an exact criterion for endpoint coupling recoverability: the source-blind Markov projection attains the unavoidable clock-error floor if and only if routes to distinct targets do not share graph states. Routes to the same target may merge without sacrificing endpoint fidelity. This characterization leads to an exact finite-state routing formulation and a legality-preserving scheduling procedure with recovery certificates. A marker-free construction demonstrates how shared edge structure can retain source distinctions, while a capacity-constrained family exhibits a sharp separation in paired error between edit orders with identical marginal error. Finally, a target-conditioned aliasing bound connects structural route design to the terminal fidelity of a learned graph-only generator. These results characterize when legal edit ordering can preserve a prescribed coupling under fixed operational costs.

title: High-dimensional two-sample testing: From optimal transport to optimal derangements
authors: Abhradipta Ghosh, Vaibhav Sherkar, Bilol Banerjee, Anil K. Ghosh
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38519v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In recent years, optimal transport has emerged as a useful framework for constructing distribution-free multivariate two-sample tests by transporting observations to a reference distribution under a suitable transportation cost. However, existing optimal transport-based tests can perform poorly in high dimension, low sample size (HDLSS) settings, and their performance depends critically on the choice of the reference distribution and transportation cost. We investigate this phenomenon and show that suitable choices can substantially improve their performance. Motivated by this analysis, we introduce a class of two-sample tests based on optimal derangements that do not require an external reference distribution. The minimum distance pairing test of Rosenbaum arises as a special case when the optimization is restricted to a subclass of derangements, thereby revealing a connection between this method and optimal transport. We propose the optimal derangement (ODER) test and its distribution-free variant, the ODER-SHC test, obtained by restricting the minimization to derangements consisting of a single Hamiltonian cycle. We establish their consistency under both HDLSS and classical large-sample asymptotic regimes. We also develop corresponding procedures based on the $L1$ distance and establish their high-dimensional consistency under conditions involving coordinate-wise energy distances. These $L1$ distance based tests can also discriminate between two high-dimensional distributions with identical first two moments but different marginal distributions. Analyses of benchmark datasets and extensive simulation studies demonstrate the performance of the proposed methods across a variety of alternatives and data settings.

title: Dimension-free exponential entropy quotients over $\mathbb{F}_2$
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38525v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $X$ be a random vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^m$, and let $X'$ be an independent copy. We prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a subspace $G$ with $\dim G\le 2^{320(1+\varepsilon)/\varepsilon}H(X)$ such that $H(q_GX)\le(1+\varepsilon)(H(q_GX+q_GX')-H(q_GX))$. In particular, the quotient entropy is at most $(1+\varepsilon)(H(X+X')-H(X))$. The coefficient is independent of the ambient dimension, and its exponential order in $1/\varepsilon$ is necessary. The structural result is a logarithmic rigidity estimate for finite weighted families of laws with averaged subspace entropy sparsity. A common variational quotient controls both a family and its convolution family without decreasing the original family's normalized mean entropy defect. Posterior families preserve averaged sparsity, and a fresh-index argument combines a local-to-global estimate with the entropic Marton theorem to increase the defect ratio at a fixed multiplicative sparsity cost. We also obtain two-input almost-additivity and concentration of moderate-doubling sets on subspace cosets at the same exponential scale. The constants are not optimized.

title: Reduced and Mixed-Precision Block Householder QR Factorization
authors: Peter Benner, Martin K\"ohler, Xiaobo Liu, Eda Oktay
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38537v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in hardware architecture have highlighted the importance of reduced-precision arithmetic for improving performance and reducing energy consumption in large-scale scientific applications. However, uniformly low-precision methods can suffer from numerical instability, especially in fundamental linear algebra routines. Mixed-precision strategies therefore play an important role in balancing efficiency, stability, and accuracy. In this paper, we focus on the block Householder QR decomposition using the WY representation and study its behavior in reduced- and mixed-precision settings. Starting from a uniform half-precision variant, we show that performing norm computations with fp32 accumulation is necessary to avoid overflow and underflow on large matrices. Based on this observation, we introduce mpWYQR, a mixed-precision algorithm that increases the precision of only selected computations and avoids most of the precision conversions required by the existing mixed-precision blocked QR algorithm (mpBQR3) introduced in [L. M. Yang, A. Fox, and G. Sanders, SIAM J. Sci. Comp., 43.3 (2021), pp. A1723--A1753]. Our analysis shows that mpWYQR accuracy is governed by low-precision unit roundoff, and that its error bound exceeds that of mpBQR3 by only a constant factor, with identical heuristic bounds. In experiments across a range of matrix sizes and condition numbers, we show that mpWYQR retains mpBQR3 accuracy while running up to $18\times$ faster and using less memory. We also discuss the performance cost of computing inner products in higher precision, and the library support needed for an efficient GPU implementation.

title: Optimality Conditions and Solution Set Characterisations of Convex Minimal Time Optimisation Problems
authors: Doan Huu Hieu, Nguyen Duy Cuong
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38553v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The paper studies convex minimisation problems involving a composition of a coordinatewise nondecreasing convex function with a finite family of nonnegative, locally Lipschitz continuous and convex functions. We establish complete dual optimality conditions and characterise the entire solution set using multipliers and subgradients associated with a given solution. The results are applied to norm optimisation problems involving minimal time functions with different convex dynamics sets and convex target sets. The sum, maximum and p-norms yield minimal time versions of the Fermat--Torricelli, Chebyshev centre and p-Fermat--Torricelli problems, respectively. Examples in finite and infinite dimensional spaces are provided to illustrate the solution set characterisations.

title: Local Hardy and bmo Spaces on Filtered Lie Groups
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38562v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a theory of local Hardy and $bmo$ spaces on a connected Lie group with polynomial growth whose Lie algebra is endowed with a filtration. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that the local Hardy spaces enjoy an appropriate atomic decomposition, are compatible with Calder\'on--Zygmund operators, and can be identified with certain Triebel--Lizorkin spaces, as it happens in the classical settings.

title: cuPDQPx: A GPU-Accelerated Restarted Halpern PDHG for Large-Scale Convex Quadratic Programming
authors: Haihao Lu, Zedong Peng, Jinwen Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.38706v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present cuPDQPx, a GPU-accelerated, factorization-free first-order solver for large-scale convex quadratic programming (QP). Building on the restarted reflected Halpern primal-dual framework of cuPDLPx, we introduce an auxiliary-variable splitting that yields explicit updates without linearizing the quadratic objective or solving inner quadratic subproblems. A preconditioned proximal point interpretation yields both sublinear and linear fixed-point residual convergence guarantees. For practical efficiency, cuPDQPx integrates diagonal preconditioning, step-size selection, adaptive restart, and adaptive primal and quadratic weight updates. cuPDQPx is implemented in C and CUDA with optimized sparse matrix-vector products, kernel fusion, and CUDA Graphs. Numerical experiments on the Maros-M\'esz\'aros collection, a convex subset of QPLIB, and synthetic large-scale QPs demonstrate that cuPDQPx has strong numerical performance at both $10^{-4}$ and $10^{-8}$ tolerances.
